sections.content: You know *porque* from A1 Unit 2. Now use it to explain why an action has happened: the reason can follow a sentence in the *pretérito perfecto*, as in *He vuelto porque ha llovido*. The verb after *porque* is conjugated normally.

items.english: I have returned because it has rained.

items.spanish: Hemos cambiado la ruta porque ha llovido.
items.english: We have changed the route because it has rained.
I have rested because I am tired.

items.spanish: Hemos decidido volver porque ha llovido.
items.english: We have decided to return because it has rained.

sections.content: Don't mix up *porque* with *por qué*: *porque* (one word, no accent) gives a reason, while *por qué* (two words, with the accent) asks a question — *He vuelto porque ha llovido* answers exactly the question *¿Por qué has vuelto?*
